verdict: Bengaluru's froth picture is essentially unchanged since July 12. No macro shift has occurred — RBI held the repo rate at 5.25% at the June MPC and the next decision comes at the Aug 3–5 MPC. Luxury-skew (~96% of Q2 launches ≥₹80L) and the Indiranagar asking-vs-guidance gap (50–80%) remain the loudest red flags, while inventory build (~15 months) and stretched affordability (35% EMI/income) sit amber; housing GNPA at 0.5% and a resilient banking system keep systemic risk contained.

indicators.name: Unsold inventory overhang
indicators.value: Bengaluru ~15 months (Q2 2026); pan-India unsold ~6.16 lakh units
indicators.note: Anarock Q2 2026: Bengaluru launches ~21,670 units (+41% YoY) vs sales ~15,285 units (+1% YoY); unsold stock ended 2025 at 64,863 units (+23% YoY). Anarock expects inventory to peak in Q3 2026 before festive absorption; no Q3 2026 report published yet.

indicators.name: Launch mix skew to luxury
indicators.note: Anarock Q2 2026 breakdown: ₹80L–1.5Cr = 27% of launches, ₹1.5–2.5Cr = 25%, above ₹2.5Cr = 22%. Only ~4% of supply catered to sub-₹80L buyers. Developers keep pivoting to premium as mid-segment demand thins.

indicators.name: EMI-to-income (affordability)
indicators.note: Knight Frank India Affordability Index H1 2026: Bengaluru EMI/income worsened marginally to 35% (from 34% in H2 2025) despite ~125 bps of cumulative easing. Home-loan rates now ~7.25–9.5% (typical ~8.0%). RBI held repo at 5.25% at June MPC; next MPC Aug 3–5, 2026 — market pricing another possible cut.
indicators.src: Knight Frank India Affordability Index H1 2026; RBI MPC June 2026

indicators.name: Housing-loan defaults (NPAs)
indicators.note: RBI Financial Stability Report June 2026: housing-loan GNPA at 0.5% (down from ~1.2% in Mar 2019); system GNPA at multi-decadal low 1.8%, projected to rise only to 1.9% by Mar 2028. Loans ≥₹50L now 44.7% of outstanding housing credit. Unsecured retail (GNPA 1.7%) flagged for watch, but housing itself is clean.

indicators.name: Asking vs registered price gap
indicators.note: Indiranagar guidance ~₹12k/sqft vs market ₹18–22k/sqft (50–83% premium). Newer corridors (Devanahalli, Hoskote) narrower at 15–25%. Karnataka doubled registration fee Aug 2025 (1%→2%); Feb 2026 hiked BBMP guidance 6–15%; a further statewide 10–15% hike is under consideration for FY27 but not yet notified. Wide gap in prime pockets remains a clear froth signal.

indicators.name: Registration volumes
indicators.value: Karnataka FY25–26 stamps revenue ~₹20,837 cr (record); Kaveri 2.0 live
indicators.note: Karnataka Stamps & Registration posted a record ~₹20,837 cr in FY25–26 (much from Bengaluru). Headline revenue is inflated by the Aug 2025 fee doubling and Feb 2026 guidance hike — transactional volume growth is softer than revenue growth. Kaveri 2.0 fully live; no monthly volume aggregate published for Jun–Jul 2026.
